Basic Annals (本紀) juan 1–30

1本紀第一太祖上 Annals 1 - Taizu Part 1 (Emperor Abaoji)903–919

The Annals of Taizu, part 1 (to the third year of Shence, 918), cover the founder's birth and wonders, his rise under the Yaolian khan, accession in 907, the brothers' rebellions of 910 to 913, and the early campaigns, embassies and building works. It is the first chapter of the founding narrative.

2本紀第二太祖下 Annals 2 - Taizu Part 2 (Emperor Abaoji)919–926

Annals 2 covers the later reign of Liao Taizu (Abaoji), from 919 to his death in 926, with a closing historians comment on the origins of the house. It records campaigns in the north and west, the conquest of Bohai and its reorganization as Dongdan, tributary arrivals, Khitan sacrifices, and the first creation of the large script. The comment sketches the ancestors from Qishou to Taizu.

3本紀第三太宗上 Annals 3 - Taizong Part 1 (Emperor Deguang)923–937

Annals of Taizong (r. 926-947), covering his early career as grand marshal, his accession in 926, and the years to 947. The entries record tours and camps, tribute and embassies, court rites, the Dingzhou and Dangxiang campaigns, and the intervention that installed Shi Jingtang as emperor of Jin.

4本紀第四太宗下 Annals 4 - Taizong Part 2 (Emperor Deguang)938–947

Annals of Emperor Taizong (Yelü Deguang), Part II, from the first year of Huitong (938) to his death in Datong 1 (947). It records the Jin's titles and the cession of the Sixteen Prefectures, the reorganization of offices, the endless tribute and embassies, the war against the Later Jin, the occupation of Bian and the emperor's death, closing with the historians' comment.

5本紀第五世宗 Annals 5 - Shizong (Emperor Ruan)947–951

Basic annals of Shizong (r. 947-951): his accession at Luancheng, the quarrel with the Dowager and Li Hu, the creation of the Northern Chancellery, the rise of the Later Zhou and the Northern Han, southern campaigns, and his murder by Chage in 951. A short historians' comment closes the juan.

6本紀第六穆宗上 Annals 6 - Muzong Part 1 (Emperor Jing)951–963

Basic annals of Muzong (r. 951-969), a year-by-year chronicle of the Yingli reign: the suppression of Chage's rebels, a steady flow of tribute from Tiegli, Bigude, Jurchen and Southern Tang, dealings with the Northern Han against the Later Zhou and the Song, frequent hunting trips and drinking, and the emperor's arbitrary killing of attendants. No historians' comment is attached.

11本紀第十一聖宗二 Annals 11 - Shengzong Part 2 (Emperor Longxu)986–987

Annals 11 covers the fourth year of Tonghe (986) of Emperor Shengzong: the Liao defeat of the Jurchen in the east, the three-pronged Song invasion and its repulse at Qigou and the Shanxi front (including the capture of Yang Ye), and the Liao counter-invasion of the Song in the winter. Between the campaigns it records rewards, tribute, rites, the imperial wedding, trials and tax remissions, and it ends with Li Jiqian's marriage alliance.

12本紀第十二聖宗三 Annals 12 - Shengzong Part 3 (Emperor Longxu)987–989

Annals 12 covers the fifth to seventh years of Tonghe (987 to 989) of Emperor Shengzong. It records the end of the winter campaign against the Song, the empress dowager's and emperor's honorific titles, tours and seasonal stays, tribute from the Xia, Uighurs, Dangxiang and Jurchen, and the Liao autumn invasion of Song territory (Zhuozhou, Yizhou, Mancheng). It also holds measures on famine, tax remission, land opening and relief, the first examinations, and Ma Dechen's remonstrance against polo.

102列傳第三十二蕭奉先　李處溫　張琳　耶律余覩 Biography 32 - Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen, Zhang Lin, Yelü Yudu

Biographies of the treacherous ministers (姦臣) Xiao Fengxian, Li Chuwen and Zhang Lin, with that of the defector Yelu Yudu. They tell how the consort clan, a false plot charge against Yudu, the death of the prince of Jin and the enthronement of Prince Chun at Yanjing helped bring on the fall of the Liao, ending with a historian comment on those ministers.

103列傳第三十三文學上 Biography 33 - Men of Letters Part 1

Biography 33, the first part of the Men of Letters, gives the lives of the scholar-official Xiao Hanjianu and of Li Huan, a former Jin official held by the Liao. Hanjianu's long reply to the decree on government, on garrison service, the western frontier and banditry, is the chapter's main matter, followed by his work on honors, the histories and the code of rites. The chapter ends with Li Huan's failed flight and release and the historian's appraisal.

104列傳第三十四文學下 Biography 34 - Men of Letters Part 2

Biography 34, the second part of the Men of Letters, gives the lives of Wang Ding, Yelu Zhao, Liu Hui, Yelu Mengjian and Yelu Guyu. Each is known for writing and counsel: Zhao's letter on the northwest border and Liu Hui's letters on the western frontier and the Song histories, Mengjian's exile and his work on the national history. A closing appraisal says men of letters are useful to government.

105列傳第三十五能吏 Biography 35 - Capable Officials

Biography 35, the capable officials (能吏): Da Gongding, Xiao Wen, Ma Renwang, Yelu Duoluwo, Yang Zunxu and Wang Tang. It records their work in office: dike levies and labor services, famine relief, treasury reform, household registration, trials and the pacifying of bandit risings, with a closing historian's appraisal. It holds the strongest labor-service evidence in the biographies (the dike levy of LS-105-0015 and the service reform of LS-105-0114).

106列傳第三十六卓行 Biography 36 - Distinguished Conduct

Biography 36, distinguished conduct (卓行): Xiao Zhala, Yelu Guannu and Xiao Pulibu, three men who gave up office for a life of reclusion. Each episode shows withdrawal from service, repeated refusals of summons or appointments, and in Pulibu's case filial devotion, study and Buddhist retreat. The historian's appraisal justifies grouping them under distinguished conduct.

107列傳第三十七列女 Biography 37 - Notable Women

Biography 37, notable women (列女): Lady Chen (wife of Xing Jian), Yelu Changge, Xiao Yixin (wife of Yelu Nu), the Xiao wife of Yelu Zhuzhe and Xiao Ruolan (wife of Yelu Zhong). It shows learned, chaste and loyal women: a mother-teacher, a counselor who wrote on government, wives who shared exile or followed their husbands in death. The closing appraisal praises their constancy; the last episodes fall in the Jin war of the 1120s.

110列傳第四十姦臣上 Biography 40 - Evil Ministers Part 1

First part of the evil ministers: Yelü Yixin, who rose under Daozong, framed Empress Xuanyi and the heir apparent, and was finally disgraced; his partisan Zhang Xiaojie; and the tools of the plot, Yelü Yange and Xiao Shisan. The chapter is the main account of the crisis over the succession in the Dakang years.

111列傳第四十一姦臣下 Biography 41 - Evil Ministers Part 2

112列傳第四十二逆臣上 Biography 42 - Rebels and Traitors Part 1

First chapter of the rebels and traitors (逆臣): Xiadi and his son Delite under Taizu, Chage and Louguo under Shizong and Muzong, Chongyuan and his son Nieliugu under Daozong, and Guge, who killed his father. It is a chapter of plots against the throne, from a usurped tribal chieftainship through the murder of an emperor to the 1063 revolt at the Luan River, with the executions that followed.

115列傳第四十五二國外記 Biography 45 - Record of the Two Foreign States: Koryo and Xi Xia

Juan 115 is the Liaoshi's external account of the two states that served the Liao: Koryo and the Xia. Each section follows the annals pattern, year by year: tribute, investitures, condolence and funeral envoys, marriages, and the Liao campaigns against Koryo (985-1019) and Xia (1049-50). The Xia section opens with a description of its customs and military levy, and the chapter ends with the historians' judgment.

Glossary juan 116–116

116國語解 Glossary of National Language

The Guoyu jie is the glossary of Khitan terms appended to the Liaoshi, arranged by the sections of the history where each term occurs. Its entries explain offices, palace guards, tribes, places, rites, titles and calendar words, with readings and meanings, and the preface says it was compiled to make these terms understandable.
